fieldValues.title: The clerk's HTTP contract is one OpenAPI 3.1 document that routes, validation and client types derive from
fieldValues.decision_question: How is the contract between clerk serve and its clients kept from drifting?
fieldValues.context: Proposed from /ship clerk#96. In srs-rust, interface drift got through three gaps: embedded types emitted as {} (srs-rust#818, #1258), client types written by hand and checked only against fixtures (ADR-011), and cross-repo checks that skip when the repos are not side by side.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: Protobuf: a second schema language beside the JSON Schema every SRS schema uses. Schemas generated from code with golden files, as srs-rust does: the route that drifted. Client types written by hand: drift between server and client is found in the browser. Do nothing: the client and server agree only by convention, as the control room and the clerk did when a missing export broke the page on 2026-10-20.
fieldValues.decision_statement: clerk/api/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1) is the single source of clerk serve's contract: the server's routes and request validation derive from it, and clients generate their types from it.
fieldValues.rationale: One source that the server and the client both derive from is the structural answer to drift; OpenAPI 3.1 is JSON Schema 2020-12, the dialect SRS already uses, and JSON is native to the browser client. The drift gates (no opaque schemas, live conformance, a version for breaking changes) are clerk#97 tests that enforce it, not part of this ruling.
fieldValues.revisit_when: When a client breaks on a service change that passed the gates, or a second transport (MCP) needs a contract the document cannot express.
fieldValues.next_steps: clerk#97 writes the spec first and its tests enforce it; srs-lab#7 generates the client types.
